metaDescription: Gas backpack leaf blowers compared on engine size, harness, weight, CFM and MPH, from 51cc homeowner units to 66cc professional machines.
expertTake: The Husqvarna 360BT is the best backpack blower here for its X-Torq engine and balanced 890 CFM, the Relxxon 52cc is the value pick for ordinary acreage, and the Husqvarna 570BTS is the professional choice. Skip backpacks if your yard takes under 15 minutes to clear: a handheld is lighter and starts faster.
introParagraphs: A backpack blower moves the engine onto a frame you wear, so its weight rides on your hips instead of in your wrist. That single change is what makes half-hour sessions practical on a larger lot, and it is why professionals almost never use handhelds for yard-sized work.

Once you accept the format, the differences are in the engine, the fan and the harness. Displacement sets the airflow ceiling, the engine design affects fuel use and emissions and the harness decides whether you can carry the machine for an hour. This guide compares those factors across homeowner and professional machines.

products.name: Husqvarna 360BT 65.6cc X-Torq Backpack
products.description:
Husqvarna's 360BT sits between homeowner and professional machines: a 65.6cc X-Torq two-cycle making 3.81 horsepower, 890 CFM and 232 MPH. X-Torq is the maker's patented engine design that cuts fuel use and emissions compared with a conventional two-stroke, which matters over hundreds of tanks.

The ventilated, load-reducing harness with wide shoulder straps spreads the weight across your back and hips. The balance between airflow and weight is why this is a common choice for landscaping crews and large properties.

It costs more than the generic 52 to 63cc blowers, and in exchange you get dealer support, parts and a proven design. Plan on a proper fuel mix, a clean air filter and a plug change each season. Fit the harness with a full tank so you feel the real carried weight before you buy.
products.bestFor: Large lots and small landscaping businesses wanting a balanced professional-leaning blower.
pros: 890 CFM and 232 MPH is a strong airflow pair
X-Torq engine cuts fuel use and emissions

products.name: Husqvarna 570BTS 66cc 4 HP Backpack
products.description:
The 570BTS is Husqvarna's commercial-grade backpack: a 66cc, 4 horsepower X-Torq engine producing 972 CFM, the highest Husqvarna number in this guide. An adjustable, offset soft-grip handle reduces strain and optimizes control for operators who blow every day.

Compared with the 360BT it adds about 9 percent more airflow and a more robust, professional build. The step-up is meaningful for a business, less so for a homeowner.

It carries the highest price tier here and the most weight. As with the other Husqvarnas, expect careful fuel mixing, clean filters and periodic plug changes. Budget for a dealer fit and a service plan, since a daily machine earns its keep through uptime.
products.bestFor: Professional crews and large properties where the blower runs daily.
pros: 972 CFM from a 4 HP X-Torq engine

products.name: Husqvarna 150BT 51cc Backpack

specList.label: Harness
specList.value: Padded with hip belt and load leveling

products.description:
The 150BT is Husqvarna's entry backpack: a 51cc two-cycle with 2.16 horsepower, a padded harness, a hip belt and a weight-leveling load system. It shares the brand's ergonomic approach with a smaller engine and a lower price tier than the 360BT.

For a half-acre to acre lot, it provides enough airflow at a comfortable weight. Compared with the generic 52cc units, you pay for the brand's service network and a better-engineered harness.

It lacks the X-Torq engine of the larger models, so fuel use and emissions are those of a conventional two-cycle. Mix fuel carefully and clean the air filter. Because its engine is smaller than the 360BT, it takes longer on wet, packed leaves.
products.bestFor: Homeowners with up to an acre who want a branded backpack.
pros: Lower tier than the larger Husqvarnas

products.name: Schröder SR-6400L 63.3cc 3.7 HP Backpack
products.description:
Schröder builds a commercial-grade backpack with a 63.3cc, 3.7 horsepower two-stroke engine and a stated air speed up to 230 MPH. At 19.5 pounds, it is lighter than many blowers with similar output, which is what extends the time you can work.

It competes with the Husqvarna 360BT on specs, though the brand has a thinner dealer network. Weight per unit of airflow is its selling point.

Expect the usual upkeep, and check parts availability before buying. Ask about spare parts and a warranty before you buy, since the dealer network is smaller. Test the harness fit with a full tank to feel the real weight.
products.bestFor: Long sessions where carried weight is the limiting factor.

products.name: VEVOR 63cc Backpack 1110 CFM 220 MPH
products.description:
VEVOR quotes 1110 CFM and 220 MPH from a 63cc two-cycle, a higher airflow figure than the Husqvarna 570BTS from a smaller engine. Treat that with skepticism: maker-measured numbers are not comparable across brands, and a 63cc engine producing more airflow than a 66cc commercial machine suggests a different measurement point.

The kit is generous, with earmuffs, a manual and a corrugated tube included. A 1.89-liter tank gives long runtime per fill, and a shock-absorbing frame with ergonomic straps carries the weight.

It is a value option for large yards, with the risks of an unproven brand. Keep the filters clean. Fit hearing protection and eye protection every session.
products.bestFor: Budget buyers who want large-yard capability and an accessory kit.
cons: Airflow claim is not comparable to others

products.name: Relxxon 52cc Backpack 550 CFM Cruise Control
products.description:
Relxxon offers a 52cc engine producing 550 CFM and 205 MPH in a 17.2-pound frame, with variable speed throttle and cruise control. Cruise control holds airflow across open ground, so you do not clamp the trigger for an hour.

A reduced-pull recoil system eases starting. Compared with the Husqvarna 150BT it has similar engine size, a lower price tier and a similar airflow class.

It is a solid value for ordinary acreage if you are comfortable with a generic brand. Mix fuel properly and keep the air filter clean. Keep a spare plug and filter on a shelf, since a budget brand may not have a nearby dealer.
products.bestFor: Half-acre to two-acre lots on a budget.
pros: 17.2 pounds is light for a backpack

products.name: PROYAMA 51.7cc Backpack 600 CFM 250 MPH
products.description:
PROYAMA quotes 600 CFM and 250 MPH from a 51.7cc engine making 1.9 horsepower at 7000 rpm. The air speed figure is the highest in this guide, higher than the 570BTS, which again illustrates why maker-measured numbers should be taken as marketing ceilings.

A ventilated breathable back pad and a self-lock trigger reduce hand fatigue, and the harness is adjustable. Those comfort details are real advantages for long jobs.

Plan for fuel mixing and check the warranty, as with any generic import. Check the harness fit over a jacket in autumn. Watch the fuel mix closely, since a hard-working 7000 rpm engine is unforgiving of poor fuel.
products.bestFor: Budget buyers who want comfort features and strong claimed speed.

buyingCriteria.explanation: A 51cc engine like the Husqvarna 150BT makes about 2.16 HP, a 65.6cc 360BT makes 3.81 HP and a 66cc 570BTS makes 4 HP. Airflow rises with displacement, but claims across brands are not comparable. Judge by engine class and brand reputation as much as by CFM. If you are choosing between two models, ask which engine a mechanic in your town can service this week. Remember that a bigger engine also means more fuel, more noise and more weight on your back.

A backpack's value is in the harness. The Schröder SR-6400L weighs 19.5 pounds and the Relxxon 52cc weighs 17.2, which matters over an hour. Look for padded straps, a hip belt and a ventilated back pad like the PROYAMA and 360BT. Wear the unit loaded with fuel for ten minutes in the store or at home before keeping it.

The X-Torq engines in the Husqvarna 360BT and 570BTS reduce fuel use and emissions compared with a conventional two-stroke. Over many tanks, the savings add up. Generic 2-cycle engines are simpler and cheaper but burn more fuel. A practical check is to read the owner's manual for the recommended fuel ratio before the first tank.

Variable speed throttles let you ease off near beds, and cruise control holds airflow across open ground. The Relxxon includes both and the PROYAMA has a self-lock trigger. Long sessions are far more tiring without them. Cruise control matters most when you are clearing wide, open ground for long stretches.

A 1.89-liter tank, as on the VEVOR, gives a long run per fill. Smaller tanks mean more stops. Runtime also depends on throttle setting, since full throttle drinks fuel. If you refuel often, a larger tank saves time; if you carry the unit far, a smaller one saves weight.

Husqvarna and Schröder offer dealer or parts networks that shorten downtime. Generic brands depend on online parts. If the blower earns money for you, service access is worth paying for. Registering the warranty on day one saves arguments later.

specDecoder.meaning: Husqvarna's two-stroke design that reduces fuel consumption and emissions. It uses a scavenging approach to keep fuel out of the exhaust. It also reduces the smell of unburned fuel during use.
A rating of engine power. Small-engine ratings vary by maker and test method. For comparison, assume a gallon of fuel adds about six pounds.
specDecoder.watchFor: 2.16 HP on the 150BT versus 4 HP on the 570BTS.

specDecoder.meaning: Air volume and air speed at the nozzle, both maker-measured. They are best compared within a brand. Use these numbers to rank, not to promise results.
specDecoder.watchFor: VEVOR claims 1110 CFM and PROYAMA 250 MPH.

specDecoder.meaning: Weight without fuel. Add fuel when estimating what you will carry. Always add the fuel weight yourself.
A lock that holds the throttle at a set position. It reduces hand fatigue.

howWeEvaluated.title: Engine and airflow
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared displacement and quoted airflow across 51 to 66cc engines, treating maker figures as ceilings. The Husqvarna 570BTS and 360BT scored highest on engine design. Quoted airflow was used only to rank, since test methods differ by maker.

howWeEvaluated.title: Harness and weight
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed harness design and carried weight. The Schröder at 19.5 pounds and the Relxxon at 17.2 earned credit for power-to-weight. We noted that a few pounds of difference becomes obvious after forty minutes of work.

howWeEvaluated.title: Controls
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at variable speed, cruise control and trigger locks, which determine comfort in long sessions. Variable speed and cruise control earned credit because they cut fatigue.

howWeEvaluated.title: Service and parts
howWeEvaluated.description: We favored Husqvarna and Schröder for service coverage, and scored generic brands cautiously. Owner feedback patterns on starting and carburetor issues shaped the scoring. Manufacturers with long service histories received a small bonus for dependability.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We separated the Relxxon as the value pick from the 570BTS as the professional pick. Value was judged against engine class, not just price.

rows: Cruise control at a low tier

cards.label: Homeowner
cards.text: The Husqvarna 150BT, Relxxon and PROYAMA use 51 to 52cc engines and suit one to two acres with a few hours of use per month.

cards.label: Professional
cards.text: The Husqvarna 360BT and 570BTS and the Schröder use 63 to 66cc engines built for daily work and dealer service.

howToChoose.note: Pick homeowner class for weekend work, professional class if the blower earns money.

howToChoose.subheading: For Wet Leaves and Debris Specifically

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Look for air speed above 200 MPH and 600 CFM or more. Wet leaves and pine needles need speed to peel off the ground.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Husqvarna 360BT at 232 MPH and the Schröder at 230 MPH lead on credible figures, and the 570BTS adds 972 CFM for volume.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Spend more if you blow for hours or professionally, which points to the Husqvarna 360BT or 570BTS.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Save if the property is under two acres. The Relxxon 52cc handles it at a lower price.

maintenance.task: Mix fuel at the correct ratio
maintenance.why: Wrong ratios cause smoke or engine damage. Use fresh fuel.
Dusty work clogs filters quickly and starves the engine.
A fouled plug is a common cold-start problem.

maintenance.task: Inspect the harness and anti-vibration mounts
maintenance.why: Worn mounts raise vibration and fatigue.

maintenance.task: Drain or stabilize fuel for storage

faq.a: Backpack for sessions beyond about 20 minutes, because the harness carries the weight. Handheld for quick jobs.

faq.q: How many CFM do I need?
faq.a: For typical residential work, 500 to 700 CFM suffices. Larger lots and heavy debris benefit from 800 or more.
Not across brands. Use them to rank within a class and rely on engine size and brand reputation.
Husqvarna's engine design that cuts fuel consumption and emissions in a two-stroke. It is on the 360BT and 570BTS.
Yes. Backpack blowers are loud, and the VEVOR includes earmuffs for that reason.

faq.q: How long will a backpack blower last?
faq.a: Many seasons with fresh fuel, clean filters and proper storage. Professional units last longest.
